'''Tamar Debora Ziegler''' ({{Langx|he|תמר ציגלר}}; born 1971) is an Israeli [[mathematician]] specializing in [[Ergodic theory]], [[Additive combinatorics]] and [[Number theory]]. She holds the Henry and Manya Noskwith Chair of [[Mathematics]] at the [[Einstein Institute of Mathematics]] at the [[Hebrew University]]. Ziegler is known for her contributions to the development of higher-order Fourier analysis and for applying methods from dynamical systems to problems in arithmetic combinatorics and number theory.

==Career==

Ziegler received her Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[Hebrew University]] under the supervision of [[Hillel Furstenberg]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=92267}}</ref> Her thesis title was “Non conventional ergodic averages”. She spent five years in the US as a postdoc at the [[Ohio State University]], the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at Princeton, and the [[University of Michigan]]. She was a faculty member at the [[Technion]] during the years 2007–2013, and joined the [[Hebrew University]] in the Fall of 2013 as a full professor.

Ziegler served as an editor of several journals. Among others she was an editor of the ''[[Journal of the European Mathematical Society]]'' (JEMS), an associate editor of the ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'', and the Editor in Chief of the ''[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]''.

==Research==
Ziegler's research lies in the interface of [[ergodic theory]] with several mathematical fields including [[combinatorics]], [[number theory]], [[algebraic geometry]] and [[theoretical computer science]].

Together with [[Ben Green (mathematician)|Ben Green]] and [[Terence Tao]], she developed the framework of [[higher-order Fourier analysis]], which connects the [[Gowers norm]]s with [[nilsequences]], and is a powerful tool for analyzing arithmetic structures in sets of integers. These ideas led to major breakthroughs in understanding linear equations in primes.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Green | first1=Ben | last2=Tao | first2=Terence | title=Linear equations in primes | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] | year=2010 | volume=171 | issue=3 | pages=1753–1850 | mr=2680398 | doi=10.4007/annals.2010.171.1753 | arxiv=math/0606088 | s2cid=119596965 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Green | first1=Ben | last2=Tao | first2=Terence | title=The Möbius function is strongly orthogonal to nilsequences | journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] | year=2012 | volume=175 | issue=2 | pages=541–566 | mr=2877066 | doi=10.4007/annals.2012.175.2.3 | arxiv=0807.1736 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| doi = 10.4007/annals.2012.176.2.11
| title = An inverse theorem for the Gowers <math>U^{s+1}[N]</math>-norm
| journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]]

==Recognition==
Ziegler won the [[Erdős Prize]] of the [[Israel Mathematical Union]] in 2011,<ref>{{cite web |title = Erdős Prize |url = https://www.imu.org.il/erdos-prize |access-date = 26 August 2026|website = IMU| language = en}}<\ref> the Bruno memorial award in 2015,<ref>{{cite web |title = About the Bruno Award — Michael Bruno Memorial Award |url = https://iias.huji.ac.il/about-bruno-award
 |access-date = 13 October 2025 |website = IIAS |language = en }}</ref> the [[Alexanderson Award]] in 2023, and the Rothschild Prize in 2024.<ref>{{cite web |title = The Rothschild Prize — Yad Hanadiv |url = https://www.yadhanadiv.org.il/rothschild-prize
 |accessdate = 13 October 2025 |website = Yad Hanadiv |language = en }}</ref> She received [[European Research Council]] Consolidator grant in 2016 and [[European Research Council]] Advanced grant in 2025.

Ziegler was the [[European Mathematical Society]] lecturer of the year in 2013, an invited sectional speaker at the 2014 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], an invited plenary speaker at the 2024 [[European Congress of Mathematics]], and an invited plenary speaker at the 2026 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref>{{cite web
 |title = Speakers — ICM 2026
 |url = https://www.icm2026.org/event/ac193975-5d24-4628-8c30-ddb23de19a8b/speakers
 |website = ICM 2026
 |access-date = 13 October 2025
 |language = en
}}</ref>

Ziegler was named [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] Simons Professor for 2016–2017.<ref>{{Cite web|last=MSRI|title=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|url=http://www.msri.org/|access-date=2021-06-07|website=www.msri.org}}</ref> She was a Distinguished Visiting Professor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 2022-23 leading the special year on Dynamics, Additive Number Theory and Algebraic Geometry]<ref>{{cite web
 |title = Special Year on Dynamics, Additive Number Theory and Algebraic Geometry — Institute for Advanced Study
 |url = https://www.ias.edu/math/events/sp/dynamics-additive-number-theory-and-algebraic-geometry
 |access-date = 13 October 2025
 |website = IAS (School of Mathematics)
 |date = 5 January 2021
 |language = en
}}</ref>

Ziegler was elected to the [[Academia Europaea]] in 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Ziegler_Tamar|title=Tamar Ziegler|work=Members|publisher=Academia Europaea|access-date=2021-12-18}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ziegler is the daughter of Zvi Ziegler, a professor of mathematics at [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web |author=<!-- not stated --> |date= |title=The annual lecture in memory of Prof. Elisha Netanyahu  |url=https://math.technion.ac.il/en/the-annual-lecture-in-memory-of-prof-elisha-netanyahu/ }}</ref>
